heading: INT. MUNICIPAL CLOCK TOWER - MECHANISM ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. MUNICIPAL CLOCK TOWER - MECHANISM ROOM - DAY
A cramped stone chamber crowded with brass gears the size of cartwheels.
A pendulum swings slowly behind a wire cage.
Dust floats in the shafts of light from a narrow slit window.
The ticking is steady, enormous, almost restful.
ARTHUR PENROSE-LIND, 60s, silver mustache, tweed jacket, kneels over a toolbox with the unhurried air of a man being paid by the hour.
His partner MIRIAM VOSS, 50s, sharp-eyed and gray-braided, sits on an upturned bucket with a ledger on her knee.
DESMOND "DEZ" OYELOWO, 30s, in a maintenance jumpsuit, oils a gear with a long-spouted can while keeping one ear on the stairwell.
Perched on the stairs, a nervous teenager, CALLUM BRIGHT, 17, holds a walkie-talkie he has not been asked to use.
Fine work, Dez. The old girl's never sounded better.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: She hasn't been oiled since Truman.
units.name: DEZ

units.text: The bank vault is directly below the east face. Four feet of brick, then the floor.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: And the pendulum shaft goes down how far?
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: Right to the ceiling of the vault annex. Nobody ever sealed it.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: Arthur nods, pulls a coil of rope from the toolbox, and measures it against his arm.
Dez sets down the oil can and checks the cage latch.
Callum shifts on the step.
The walkie-talkie crackles with static, and he fumbles it to silence.
Sorry.
units.name: CALLUM

units.text: Nothing to be sorry for, lad. Nothing at all.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: Thursday, then. After the noon chime, before the council tour.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: The council tour is at one.
units.name: DEZ

units.text: Then we have forty minutes. Plenty.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: The clock gathers itself and strikes the quarter hour.
The gears turn.
Nobody flinches.
